- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days if sentiment remains neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment is positive but price is falling, model may lag; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast if sentiment > 0.10 and price > 75.
- Model underestimates downward trends when sentiment is negative and price is falling; increase forecast by 2–5% if sentiment < -0.30 and price < 70.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates mean reversion; reduce forecast by 3–5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive and price is above 75.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before applying sentiment-adjusted correction.
